_help: Add a new 'set' each week. The game shows the newest set whose 'start' date has arrived, so you can load several weeks ahead. answer = index of the correct option (0 = first). 'fact' shows after each question. Players see answers after playing, so keep each week's set fresh.

questions.q: In what year did the Boston Tea Party take place?
questions.fact: On December 16, 1773, colonists dumped 342 chests of tea into Boston Harbor.

questions.q: Which is the oldest public park in the United States?
questions.fact: Boston Common dates to 1634, when it was used as shared grazing land for cattle.

questions.q: The Boston Marathon is run on which holiday?
questions.fact: Patriots' Day falls on the third Monday in April in Massachusetts.

questions.q: What's the nickname of Fenway Park's left-field wall?
questions.fact: The Green Monster stands about 37 feet tall.

questions.q: Which ship, docked in Charlestown, is the world's oldest commissioned warship still afloat?
questions.fact: "Old Ironsides" was launched in 1797.

questions.q: Roughly how long is the Freedom Trail?
questions.fact: The red-brick line connects 16 historic sites.

questions.q: What is the oldest public school in America, founded in 1635?
questions.fact: Boston Latin School predates Harvard by a year.

questions.q: The town of Winthrop is named after John Winthrop. Who was he?
options: Founding governor of the Massachusetts Bay Colony
questions.fact: John Winthrop led the Puritans who settled Boston in 1630.

questions.q: Where can you ride the famous Swan Boats?
questions.fact: The Swan Boats have been run by the same family since 1877.

questions.q: In what year did the Great Molasses Flood hit Boston's North End?
questions.fact: A storage tank burst in January 1919, sending a wave of molasses through the streets.

questions.q: Boston's nickname "Beantown" comes from what?
options: A famous bean farm in Roxbury
questions.fact: Boston was a hub of the molasses trade, and baked beans became a local staple.

questions.q: In what year did Paul Revere make his famous midnight ride?
questions.fact: The ride took place on the night of April 18, 1775.

questions.q: "One if by land, two if by sea" referred to what, hung in the Old North Church?
questions.fact: Two lanterns signaled that British troops were crossing the Charles by boat.

questions.q: Logan International Airport is in which Boston neighborhood?
questions.fact: Logan sits on filled land between East Boston and Winthrop.

questions.q: The Bunker Hill Monument actually stands on which hill?
questions.fact: Most of the 1775 battle was fought on Breed's Hill, but the name stuck.

questions.q: The Massachusetts State House dome is covered in what?
questions.fact: The dome was covered in gold leaf in 1874. It was painted gray during WWII to hide it from possible attacks.

questions.q: In what year did Fenway Park open?
questions.fact: Fenway opened in April 1912, days after the Titanic sank.

questions.q: Where is the "Make Way for Ducklings" statue?
questions.fact: The bronze Mrs. Mallard and her eight ducklings were installed in 1987.

questions.q: The Zakim Bridge crosses which river?
questions.fact: Its full name is the Leonard P. Zakim Bunker Hill Memorial Bridge.

questions.q: Boston opened America's first subway in 1897. Under which street?
questions.fact: The Tremont Street Subway is still in use today as part of the Green Line.
